add_characteristics.text: Please Please Please, examined whole: the chorus runs from politest to bluntest (tripled polite title, a petty makeup stake, a line ranking heartbreak below ego, the profane word last); Carpenter says that passage was the most deliberately shaped and its last word an ad lib with the melody pushed lower.
add_characteristics.evidence: SP-F2 documented_statement; SP-F3 observable_feature via tool paraphrase

add_characteristics.text: A fantasy verse is set apart harmonically (Antonoff: A to C on verse 2) and the return pops the bubble; the fantasy is retracted as a joke with some truth in it.
The narrator is built to be pitied and feared at once (Antonoff's Dolly model: sad but not to be messed with).

coverage: Now rests on one whole-song examination (Please Please Please, via the Song Exploder transcript and a press print of the lyric, both seen only through tool extraction) plus process accounts for Espresso and Manchild. Does not cover Taste, Tears or any Man's Best Friend lyric as a whole work; no official lyric presentation was accessed.

add_characteristics.text: Ain't In LA, examined whole: a pronoun ladder, third-person portrait (she) in verse 1, 'you' in the second pre-chorus and verse 2, the first 'I' only in the chorus; a tribute to her mother turned into an address to other girls.
add_characteristics.evidence: SP-F8 observable_feature via tool paraphrase; SP-S8 documented_statement

add_characteristics.text: The title names only the place it rejects; LA is the lyric's only named place and the affirmed place is never named, which listeners filled with their hometowns and critics wanted filled with Bratislava.
Refuses LA's monopoly from inside (she lives there and likes it) rather than attacking the city.
A second voice (Theron Thomas, pitched down per press) carries a status-image refrain with no 'I' and stands in for a bridge.
add_characteristics.evidence: SP-F11 observable_feature, low confidence on its meaning

coverage: Per-track writer credits for all 11 PRIMA tracks now read from Qobuz distributor credits (SP-S3), replacing the uncited Wikipedia table; they match it, including Therapy's unusual producer list. One unverified anomaly: the extract shows no Jergová writing credit on KGB. Ain't In LA examined whole via Capital FM's printed lyric seen only through tool paraphrase; no co-writer statement (Billboard Thomas feature blocked). Still does not cover ballad craft, or Nicole Kidman as a whole work.
